title: An open equivalence relation on a flat presentation has etale quotient
statement: Work over a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space], algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and stacks in groupoids, their morphisms and $2$-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Let $Y$ be an algebraic space over $S$ and let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over $Y$, with the test-point laws of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Suppose $U\to Y$ is flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and $(t,s):R\to U\times_YU$ is an open immersion, meaning that each scheme base change is an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $[U/R]$ be the fppf stackification of its test-point groupoid [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description], and let $U/R$ be the fppf sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $T\mapsto U(T)/R(T)$. Then $[U/R]$ is equivalent to the discrete stack of the algebraic space $U/R$, and the induced map $U/R\to Y$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Flatness, local finite presentation and etaleness for algebraic spaces are tested on etale scheme charts.

proof.text: Put $P=U\times_YU$ and $j=(t,s):R\to P$. By the hypothesis, every scheme base change of $j$ is an open subscheme inclusion, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Thus $j$ is representable etale in the scheme-test sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The two projections $P\to U$ are base changes of $U\to Y$; they are flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. That node also makes $j$ flat and locally of finite presentation (etale implies smooth implies both), and makes their composites $s,t$ flat and locally of finite presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-groupoid-algebraic-quotient] to the given test-point groupoid, now with flat locally finitely presented $s,t$. It gives an algebraic stack $\mathcal Q=[U/R]$, a representable surjective flat locally finitely presented map $p:U\to\mathcal Q$, and the canonical equivalence $R\simeq U\times_{\mathcal Q}U$, with its two projections $s,t$. The groupoid laws and all size bounds are exactly the hypotheses of the item.

source.place: Tag 0DU1 (lemma-quotient-etale), first proof sentence; criteria.tex Tags 06FI and 06FH

proof.text: An open immersion is injective on test-scheme sections: after base change along a test section of its target there is at most one lift to the resulting open subscheme. Hence $R(T)\to(U\times_YU)(T)$ is injective. For $u\in U(T)$ the preceding self-relation equivalence identifies automorphisms of $p(u)$ with arrows in $R(T)$ from $u$ to itself; there is exactly one, since the identity exists. Every object of $\mathcal Q(T)$ is fppf locally isomorphic to such a $p(u)$ by [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. Its automorphisms are therefore locally identities, and are globally identities because isomorphism presheaves of a stack are sheaves. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-setoid-space] to obtain an algebraic space $X$ and an equivalence $\mathcal Q\simeq h_X$. The structural map to $Y$ descends from the groupoid's given map to $Y$, by the stackification extension property, so $p:U\to X$ is over $Y$ and $R\simeq U\times_XU$.

source.place: Tag 0DU1 (lemma-quotient-etale), second proof sentence, no automorphisms, and the equality with the sheaf quotient

proof.text: Write $F(T)=U(T)/R(T)$ and $A=F^\#$. The map $U\to X$ induces $F\to X$ and hence $\alpha:A\to X$ by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], since $X$ is an fppf sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Conversely, for $x\in X(T)$ choose an fppf cover on which it is represented by $u_i\in U(T_i)$, using [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] and the equivalence above. On overlaps the two representatives have equal images in $X$, hence give a section of $U\times_XU=R$. Their images in $A$ agree, so glue uniquely. This defines $\beta:X\to A$, independently of the cover and representatives: on a common refinement the same relation argument gives equality. It commutes with base change by restricting these representatives. Locally $\alpha\beta(x)=x$, so this holds globally. Also $\beta\alpha$ agrees with the identity after $F\to A$; uniqueness in the sheafification universal property makes it the identity on $A$. Thus $A\cong X$, compatibly over $Y$, proving $[U/R]\simeq h_{U/R}$.

source.place: Tag 0DU1 (lemma-quotient-etale), second proof sentence, identification with U/R, with the universal-property argument written out

proof.text: The map $p:U\to X$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation by Step 2, and its composite with $f:X\to Y$ is the given flat locally finitely presented $U\to Y$. The source-local clause of [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent], taking the identity target cover of $Y$, therefore proves that $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Identities are surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. No surjectivity of $U\to Y$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0DU1 (lemma-quotient-etale), third proof sentence, descent of flatness and local finite presentation

proof.text: Consider $q=p\times_Yp:U\times_YU\to X\times_YX$. Factor it as $U\times_YU\to X\times_YU\to X\times_YX$, first applying $p$ to the first factor and then to the second. These maps are respectively the base changes of $p$ along $X\times_YU\to X$ (first projection) and $X\times_YX\to X$ (second projection). Thus both, and their composite $q$, are surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Pulling back $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_YX$ by $q$ gives $U\times_XU\to U\times_YU$, hence precisely $j:R\to U\times_YU$: on test schemes the pullback is a pair $(u,v)$ whose images in $X$ agree. All these fibre products are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Since $j$ is an open immersion, target descent along $q$ in [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent] makes $\Delta_f$ an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 0DU1 (lemma-quotient-etale), cartesian diagonal diagram and its omitted product-cover detail

proof.text: Local finite presentation implies local finite type by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Consequently [lem-sfb-space-unramified-open-diagonal] applied to Step 6 makes $f$ unramified. To finish, choose a surjective etale scheme chart $V\to Y$ and a surjective etale scheme chart $W\to X\times_YV$, as in [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], their base change and composite give a surjective etale map $W\to X$. The scheme map $h:W\to V$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test], and unramified by [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts]. It is etale by the conjunction defining [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The etale clause of [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts] now gives that $f$ is etale.

lean.statement: theorem open_relation_etale_quotient {S : Scheme.{u}} {Y U R : AlgebraicSpace S} (p : U ⟶ Y) (s t : R.obj.obj ⟶ U.obj.obj) (e : U.obj.obj ⟶ R.obj.obj) (i : R.obj.obj ⟶ R.obj.obj) (c : Limits.pullback s t ⟶ R.obj.obj) (hY : t ≫ p.hom.hom = s ≫ p.hom.hom) (hflat : MapIsFlat p) (hlfp : MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation p) (hopen : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ a ↦ IsOpenImmersion a.left) (pullback.lift t s hY)) (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli U.obj.obj) F) (presentation : SpaceGroupoidQuotientPresentation s t e i c F a) : ∃ (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ Y) (q : U.obj.obj ⟶ X.obj.obj) (E : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli X.obj.obj) F), E.toFunctor.IsEquivalence ∧ Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso ((discreteModuliMap q).comp E) a) ∧ q ≫ f.hom.hom = p.hom.hom ∧ (∃ η : sheafify (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (coequalizer s t ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}) ≅ X.obj.obj ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}, Functor.whiskerRight (coequalizer.π s t) uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} ≫ toSheafify (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (coequalizer s t ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}) ≫ η.hom = Functor.whiskerRight q uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}) ∧ MapIsLocally (@Etale) f
